answer: A protocol sets verification cost far above submission cost. Each identity posts a cheap claim, but validation requires a proof of sequential work tied to the claim hash and epoch seed, not parallelizable or batchable. A thousand cloned keys face a thousand sequential computations with no shortcut. The saffron ease of submission draws clones, yet the ferrous weight of per-key verification grinds each separately. Unlike a stake paid once for all clones, this cost is per identity per epoch and never pools. Across the lagoon of unbatchable checks, each clone is as costly as the first.
